Bounded deterministic implementation order: use one handler-owned typed continuation operation to read the authoritative exact binding and current generation, carry an explicitly separate governing order, persist immutable stored-message bytes and digest, perform a fresh CAS, record actual current/supersession bookends, and mechanically return distinct create/ack/result receipt coordinates with timestamped raw evidence. Reject mismatched identities before mutation and preserve stable retry identity. Do not reconstruct native identifiers or status from Board prose. AIV/MCP integration remains deferred.

Acceptance: different historical and governing orders enroll without overwriting binding; a CAS predecessor cannot be emitted as resulting current generation; result receipt fields reject create receipts; post-enrollment readback proves the exact current record or returns a fresh structured conflict rather than a stale-selector incident. Synthetic isolated tests only until separately authorized; no live fixture, watcher, provider, network, or deployment change.

Accountability: db-handler owns all item/database reads and writes; lead-recovery coordinates. This intake records a bounded durable bug and requires a separately saved work order before implementation.

value.title: Pause project and explicitly resume with a fresh team
value.description:
Owner request #6377 (verbatim): “OK -- I have a feature that we really need. Maybe we can test it out. We currently have no way to pause a project. That is to say to fire the entire current team but we keep the project, right?”

Bounded objective: add explicit Pause project and explicit fresh-team Resume while preserving the project and all durable history/evidence.

Acceptance:
- Explicit Pause stops/dismisses every current project team member, including lead and database handler, with exact-run durable cleanup receipts.
- Project, history, bugs/features, unfinished work, and source/result evidence remain intact; no false completion.
- Paused projects cannot wake, schedule, or admit workers automatically.
- UI distinguishes paused with cleanup pending from fully paused.
- Repeated/lost-response retries are idempotent and cannot double-close, kill replacement runs, or affect unrelated sessions/projects.
- Useful long-lived services follow existing lifecycle ownership rules.
- Explicit Resume starts a fresh team with verified retained handoff, preserving former identities/history and never silently resurrecting closed runs; reuse existing launch/retry controls where possible.
- Demonstrate pause and explicit fresh-team resume on an isolated synthetic project with preserved history before any live use.

Exclusions: do not pause Tailterm Development or any live user task/profile; no Files work; no TrueNAS/Tailscale/network changes; no unrelated closure; deploy only TailOS and appropriate Mini preview under bounded release evidence. Preserve ordinary keep-handler-available behavior for open unpaused work. Check file ownership and overlapping lifecycle branches before edits.

Assistant-proposed Resume default from owner clarification #6381 (not a verbatim owner decision): Resume opens the existing team chooser, preselecting the previous team when available, then launches fresh identities with retained project handoff. Closed/old sessions are never automatically resurrected. Keep this within pause/resume lifecycle and existing launch UI; do not create a new team-management framework.

limitations: Roster endpoint is unpaginated by server contract; no invented cursor/cutoff.
